_what: The numbers and names tools/publish-an-engine-release uses. `signing_domain` is the first line of the text each release's Ed25519 signature covers (the engine's release-feed reader, engine job J1, checks the same text). `keep_releases` is how many entries feed.json holds at most; an older entry leaves with its tar.gz. `binary` is the engine program cargo builds and the tar.gz holds beside the repository's `product_folder`. `extra_binaries` are the repository's other programs that go in the Linux releases under `extra_binaries_folder` (product/bin: an unpacker that predates them takes only the root program and product/) (the host and the cross-built Linux target); the Mac program holds `binary` alone. `feed_file` is the feed's name in the feed folder. `commit_pattern` and `target_pattern` are the only commit ids and rust target triples a path is made from. `urgent_trailer` is the commit-message trailer that marks a release urgent (`Release-Urgent: true`). `key_file_mode` is the signing key file's mode (0400); a key file anyone else can read is refused. `private_input_bytes_at_most` bounds what descriptors 3 and 4 may hold. `push_body_bytes_at_most` bounds one push delivery (GitHub caps a delivery at 25 MB). `build_timeout_ms` and `git_timeout_ms` bound one build and one git call. `parallel_builds` is how many of a commit's targets build at once (the host, the Mac and each cross target; each builds in its own folder under the work folder). `on_builder` is where install puts everything on the builder: the system user that builds and signs, its work folder, the feed folder Caddy serves, the signing key, the SSH key git reads a repository named by an ssh:// or git@ URL with (made on the builder; its public half is answered, to add to the repository as a read-only deploy key) and that SSH connection's known hosts, the tool's own files, the config, the receiver's state, and the encrypted credentials. `feed_path` is where Caddy serves the feed folder under the builder's name; `push_path` is where GitHub sends push deliveries; `receiver_port` is the receiver's port on 127.0.0.1. `catch_up_minutes` is how often the receiver compares the branch's tip with the feed (it also checks once at start), and `attempts_at_most` how many publish runs a commit gets from that check before it waits for a push. `entry_path` is where another builder (one per target it builds for) POSTs its signed release: the tar.gz as the body, its entry as base64 JSON in the `entry_header` header, the body at most `entry_body_bytes_at_most` (the engine's own `release_body_max_bytes`). `feed_lock_wait_ms` is how long a publish or accept waits for another one adding its entry to the feed. `node_major_at_least` is the Node.js the builder needs (the content identity's BLAKE3 module needs 20.19 or later); `node_dist` is where install fetches it when the builder has none, checked against that folder's SHASUMS256.txt. `rustup_url` installs the rust toolchain for the builder user when it has no cargo; the repository's own rust-toolchain file then picks the version.

kinds.what: The engine program: cargo builds `binary` for the builder's own rust target and the release roads, packed with the repository's product/ folder; the target is the host line of rustc -vV.
The Workshop's tools tree: nothing is built; the commit's git archive under one top folder (install strips it; the pax comment holds the commit), gzipped; one entry for the whole tree.

The MCP forwarder program: cargo builds trillion-mcp-forwarder alone for the builder's own rust target; the tar.gz holds the binary at its root and nothing else (no product/ folder). A relay follows this feed. Its tar.gz sits under url_folder beside the engine's, so the two never share a path. No Mac and no cross targets.

The Mac app's signed release (pack provided-files: the request names the files, each checked for its length and BLAKE3 and published under its basename, one signed entry per file): nothing is built here; the DMG is Trillion-<build>.dmg and its update record Trillion-update.json, both named by their basename (no url_folder), so the entry's url is that basename and resolves to the app's download path. Its target is the Mac's own triple, which the engine's Mac road also names: the kind's own feed keeps the two apart.

A computer's product settings file (computer/product-settings.json of the product's repository): nothing is built; its bytes are the file, stored under url_folder named by their BLAKE3 identity, so a place that holds the same identity holds the same bytes. The entry's url is that relative path, not https.

darwin._what: The Mac targets the builder cross-builds itself, from Linux, into the same feed (publish-an-engine-release.mjs `publishDarwin`). `targets` are the only Mac targets it takes, and the build is `cargo zigbuild --release --bin <binary> --target <target>` with SDKROOT at `sdk_folder` (a macOS SDK install sends from the person's computer: its frameworks hold Security and CoreFoundation, which zig does not ship) MACOSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET `deployment_target` (the Mac app's own, trillion-apps macos/project.yml). The program is then signed by `rcodesign sign` with the Developer ID identity, hardened runtime (`code_signature_flags`), a secure timestamp from `timestamp_url`, the identifier `binary`, and no entitlements (the app's own engine is signed the same way: trillion-apps scripts/release-macos-app.sh, `entitlements_by_basename` {}). `credentials` names the two systemd credentials that hold the identity (a PKCS#12 file) and its password: install encrypts them with the builder's host key, the receiver's unit opens them under $CREDENTIALS_DIRECTORY, and rcodesign reads them by path, so no value is in argv, a log or this file. Before an entry is signed, `rcodesign print-signature-info` must show the hardened runtime, the request's team in the leaf, the Developer ID Application extension `developer_id_oid` and an Apple root: the requirement trillion-apps CarriedCode.checkRelease holds a release to. `zig_folder` is the venv install puts zig in, from the ziglang wheel `zig_wheel`, pinned by version and each machine's sha256; `cargo_zigbuild` and `apple_codesign` are the crate versions install builds for the builder user.
